title: 462. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Identifying Fundamental Period from Harmonics
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Period of a fundamental with its second harmonic
questions.learningObjective: Find the fundamental period of a sum of a sinusoid and its second harmonic.
questions.question: What is the fundamental period of \(f(t)=\sin t+\sin 2t\)?
questions.explanation: The terms have periods \(2\pi\) and \(\pi\). The sum repeats when both terms have completed whole numbers of cycles, which first happens after \(2\pi\). The value \(\pi\) is a period of \(\sin 2t\) only; \(\sin t\) changes sign after \(\pi\).
questions.hint: Find the smallest time that is a whole number of periods for every term.

questions.concept: Period when both angular frequencies are even
questions.learningObjective: Find the fundamental period when the angular frequencies share a common factor.
questions.question: What is the fundamental period of \(f(t)=\sin 2t+\sin 4t\)?
questions.explanation: The terms have periods \(\pi\) and \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). Both repeat after \(\pi\), and this is the smallest such time, because \(\sin 2t\) does not repeat after \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). Equivalently, the fundamental angular frequency is the greatest common divisor of \(2\) and \(4\), which is \(2\), giving period \(\frac{2\pi}{2}=\pi\).
questions.hint: The fundamental angular frequency is the greatest common divisor of the angular frequencies of the terms.

questions.learningObjective: Find the fundamental period when the angular frequencies have no common factor.
questions.question: What is the fundamental period of \(f(t)=\sin 2t+\cos 3t\)?
questions.explanation: The angular frequencies \(2\) and \(3\) have greatest common divisor \(1\), so the fundamental angular frequency is \(1\) and the period is \(2\pi\). In \(2\pi\) the first term completes \(2\) cycles and the second completes \(3\). The value \(\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{2\pi}{6}\) uses the least common multiple \(6\) of the frequencies, which is the wrong combination.
questions.hint: Use the greatest common divisor of the angular frequencies, not their least common multiple.

questions.learningObjective: Find the fundamental period when no term has the fundamental frequency.
questions.question: What is the fundamental period of \(f(t)=\sin 4t+\sin 6t\)?
questions.explanation: The greatest common divisor of the angular frequencies \(4\) and \(6\) is \(2\), so the fundamental angular frequency is \(2\) and the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{2}=\pi\). The terms are the second and third harmonics of this fundamental, even though no term \(\sin 2t\) is present. The time \(2\pi\) is also a period, but it is not the smallest one.
questions.hint: The signal can repeat faster than \(2\pi\) if all angular frequencies share a common factor.

questions.learningObjective: Find the fundamental frequency of a signal from the frequencies of its components.
questions.question: A periodic signal consists of components at \(200\text{ Hz}\), \(300\text{ Hz}\), and \(500\text{ Hz}\) only. What is its fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: The fundamental frequency is the largest frequency of which every component is a whole-number multiple, that is, the greatest common divisor of \(200\), \(300\), and \(500\), which is \(100\text{ Hz}\). The components are the second, third, and fifth harmonics. The lowest component, \(200\text{ Hz}\), cannot be the fundamental because \(300\) is not a multiple of \(200\).
questions.hint: Find the greatest common divisor of the component frequencies.

questions.learningObjective: Find the period of a sum from the periods of its two components.
questions.question: A signal is the sum of two sinusoids with periods \(2\text{ s}\) and \(3\text{ s}\). What is the fundamental period of the signal?
questions.explanation: The sum repeats when both components have completed whole numbers of cycles. The smallest such time is the least common multiple of \(2\) and \(3\), which is \(6\text{ s}\): the first component completes \(3\) cycles and the second completes \(2\). After \(1\text{ s}\) neither component has completed a cycle.
questions.hint: Look for the smallest time that is a whole-number multiple of both periods.

questions.concept: Period from angular frequencies with pi
questions.learningObjective: Find the fundamental period of a sum whose terms have rational periods.
questions.question: What is the fundamental period of \(f(t)=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)+\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)\)?
questions.explanation: The first term has period \(\frac{2\pi}{\pi/2}=4\), and the second has period \(\frac{2\pi}{\pi/3}=6\). The least common multiple of \(4\) and \(6\) is \(12\), so the fundamental period is \(12\). The value \(24=4\cdot 6\) is a period but not the smallest one.
questions.hint: Compute each period, then take their least common multiple rather than their product.

questions.learningObjective: Find the fundamental period of a signal from two component frequencies.
questions.question: A periodic signal has components at \(150\text{ Hz}\) and \(250\text{ Hz}\) only. What is its fundamental period?
questions.explanation: The fundamental frequency is the greatest common divisor of \(150\) and \(250\), which is \(50\text{ Hz}\). The fundamental period is \(\frac{1}{50}=0.02\text{ s}\). In that time the components complete \(3\) and \(5\) cycles. The time \(\frac{1}{150}\text{ s}\) is the period of the lower component alone; the \(250\text{ Hz}\) component completes only \(\frac{5}{3}\) of a cycle in it.
questions.hint: Find the fundamental frequency first, then take its reciprocal.

questions.concept: A sum that is not periodic
questions.learningObjective: Recognise that a sum of sinusoids with an irrational frequency ratio has no period.
questions.question: Is \(f(t)=\sin t+\sin\left(\sqrt{2}\,t\right)\) a periodic function?

options.label: A
options.text: No, because the ratio of the two angular frequencies is irrational.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, with period \(2\pi\), because \(\sin t\) has period \(2\pi\).

questions.explanation: A sum of two sinusoids is periodic only if some time \(P\) is a whole number of periods for both terms, which requires the ratio of their angular frequencies to be rational. Here the ratio is \(\sqrt{2}\), which is irrational, so no common period exists. After \(2\pi\) the first term repeats, but \(\sin\left(\sqrt{2}(t+2\pi)\right)\ne\sin\left(\sqrt{2}\,t\right)\) in general.
questions.hint: Ask whether the two periods have a common whole-number multiple.

questions.learningObjective: Find the fundamental period when the angular frequencies are fractions.
questions.question: What is the fundamental period of \(f(t)=\sin\left(\frac{3t}{2}\right)+\cos\left(\frac{5t}{4}\right)\)?
questions.explanation: Write the angular frequencies with a common denominator: \(\frac{6}{4}\) and \(\frac{5}{4}\). Their greatest common divisor is \(\frac{1}{4}\), so the fundamental angular frequency is \(\frac{1}{4}\) and the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{1/4}=8\pi\). In \(8\pi\) the terms complete \(6\) and \(5\) cycles. After \(4\pi\) the first term has completed \(3\) cycles, but the second only \(2.5\), so \(4\pi\) is not a period.
questions.hint: Express both angular frequencies as multiples of one common fraction.
